summary.title: TAPS: Task Aware Proposal Distributions for Speculative Sampling

setting_and_object.category: Empirical study / Mechanism (with an inference-time composition method)

details: Speculative decoding drafters are typically trained on generic corpora (e.g. ShareGPT), so the effect of the draft training distribution on proposal quality is under-studied.
Given several specialized drafters, it is unclear whether to mix their training data, merge them in weight space, or compose them at inference time.

A controlled study showing that draft training data determines task-specific specialization in speculative decoding acceptance, plus two inference-time composition schemes that keep specialists separate: confidence routing (pick the draft tree with higher mean node confidence) and merged-tree verification (pack both specialists' draft trees under a shared root with ancestry-preserving masks and depth-based position ids, verified in one target pass).

Both composition schemes provably preserve the target model's output distribution (losslessness), since cross-subtree attention is masked and routing depends only on pre-verification draft-side statistics.
Verifier fixed to Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct; drafter is a one-layer LLaMA-style decoder, hidden size 4096, ~0.8B params, sharing tokenizer/vocabulary with the target.
Two speculative backbones: HASS and EAGLE-2; composition only within a backbone.
Hardware: single node with four A100 GPUs.
20 epochs, lr 3e-5, batch size 8; HASS uses top-K distillation with K=10, loss weight 1.0, three forward-alignment steps.
Benchmarks: MT-Bench (chat) plus GSM8K, MATH-500, SVAMP (reasoning), at temperatures 0 and 1.
Primary metric: average acceptance length under lossless speculative decoding; also acceptance rate by speculative depth (1-5) and draft/verifier entropy for accepted vs rejected tokens.
Seven draft variants per backbone: MathInstruct, ShareGPT, Mixed 35k+35k, Mixed 70k+70k, Averaged, Confidence Routed, Merged Trees.
Weight-space averaging of the two specialist checkpoints, theta = lambda*theta_math + (1-lambda)*theta_chat with lambda=0.5 in main table plus a lambda sweep.
Confidence routing: score each specialist's tree by mean node confidence, verify only the winner.
Merged-tree verification: concatenate non-root nodes of both trees, remap indices, ancestor-preserving attention mask, depth-based position ids; larger tree per verifier call.
Entropy-based routing used as an alternative routing signal for diagnosis.
Assumption of lossless verification for any valid packed tree; Lemma that mixtures over valid random trees stay lossless.

Lemma on verifier invariance under masked concatenation (transformer logits on an index set unchanged if tokens, positions, within-set mask match and no attention leaves the set), used to prove merged-tree validity.

key_findings.finding: Draft training distribution, not just architecture, determines speculative decoding acceptance: drafters specialize to their training domain.
key_findings.evidence: At temperature 0 with HASS, ShareGPT-trained drafts beat MathInstruct on MT-Bench (3.98 vs 2.90) while MathInstruct wins on GSM8K (5.02 vs 4.09) and MATH-500 (5.35 vs 3.98); the same ordering holds for EAGLE-2 (MT-Bench 3.57 vs 2.54, and MathInstruct best on GSM8K/MATH-500/SVAMP).

key_findings.finding: Specialists should be composed at inference time, not merged in weight space; merged-tree verification gives the highest acceptance length overall.
key_findings.evidence: Averaged checkpoints are the weakest variants (average acceptance length 2.34-2.62 across backbones/temperatures) and the lambda interpolation sweep is unstable, while confidence routing reaches 4.80 (HASS) and 4.63 (EAGLE-2) and merged trees reach 5.11 (HASS) and 5.02 (EAGLE-2) at temperature 0, staying best at temperature 1 (4.75 / 4.57).

key_findings.finding: Confidence is a far better routing signal than entropy, though entropy remains a diagnostic of rejection.
key_findings.evidence: Confidence routing selects the MathInstruct drafter for 90.8% of GSM8K, 97.0% of MATH-500, 93.0% of SVAMP and ShareGPT for 81.2% of MT-Bench, whereas entropy routing yields near-balanced splits (52.5-62.4%); separately, rejected tokens show consistently higher draft entropy than accepted tokens for both backbones.

key_findings.finding: Mixed-data training improves robustness but larger mixtures are not uniformly better across decoding temperatures.
key_findings.evidence: HASS Mixed 70k+70k is the best trained checkpoint at temperature 0 (5.18 average) but drops to 3.69 at temperature 1, below Mixed 35k+35k (4.29); EAGLE-2 shows the same reversal (4.48 vs 3.26 at temperature 1, where 35k+35k gives 3.81).

key_findings.finding: Acceptance behavior is depth-dependent: shallow depths favor broad coverage from mixed data while deeper positions increasingly favor the task-matched specialist.
key_findings.evidence: In depth tables, Mixed 35k+35k has the highest depth-1 average acceptance (e.g. 93.7% for EAGLE-2 at temperature 0) but MathInstruct dominates at depth 5 on reasoning tasks (e.g. 76.4% GSM8K, 81.5% MATH-500 vs 61.9%/70.6% for the mixture).
